drivingQuestion: Does residency require twelve months or thirty days?
outcomeNote: the contradiction is completed and resolved in the next unit

segments.he: וְכַמָּה יְהֵא בָּעִיר וִיהֵא כְּאַנְשֵׁי הָעִיר וְכוּ׳. וּרְמִינְהִי: הַחַמֶּרֶת וְהַגַּמֶּלֶת הָעוֹבֶרֶת מִמָּקוֹם לְמָקוֹם, וְלָנָה בְּתוֹכָהּ וְהוּדְּחָה עִמָּהֶן, הֵן בִּסְקִילָה, וּמָמוֹנָן פָּלֵט.
segments.en: § The mishna teaches: «And how long» must one live «in the city to be» considered «like» one of «the people of the city?» Twelve months. «And we raise a contradiction» from what is taught in a baraita: In the case of «a donkey caravan or a camel caravan that was journeying from place to place, and it lodged inside» an idolatrous city, «and its» members «were led astray» along «with» the other residents of the city, and they too engaged in idol worship, «they,» the members of the caravan, are liable to death «by stoning» like ordinary individual idolaters, «and their property escapes» destruction, i.e., they are not treated like the residents of an idolatrous city, who are liable to death by the sword and whose property is destroyed.

moves.summary: baraita on a caravan in an idolatrous city

edges.cueHe: וכמה יהא בעיר ויהא כאנשי העיר וכו׳

edges.about: the mishna requires twelve months to count as a townsman while the baraita treats thirty days as residency

positions.claim: twelve months makes one like the townspeople
caravan members who merely lodged are stoned individually and their property escapes

unresolved.issue: the baraita's thirty-day clause that actually creates the contradiction sits in the next sugya
